Earlier this year, Apple closed off part of the Apple Park Visitor Center, citing "improvements to our store."

The space has now reopened, and the biggest change is Apple removing the augmented reality experience that used custom iPads to let visitors see Apple Park.

When the Apple Park Visitor Center opened to the public in 2017, Apple promoted the AR experience this way:

Using augmented reality technology, a three-dimensional model of the campus comes to life before your eyes, inviting visitors to explore Apple Park in an immersive and interactive way. Visitors can learn about the world's largest naturally ventilated building, and see one of the largest onsite solar installations in the world. Visitors can also choose to lift the entire roof to peek at the layout of the interior collaboration spaces.

Before this change, the Apple Park Visitor Center was divided into three areas: an AR exhibit, a traditional Apple Store, and a cafe.

Apple has now retired the AR exhibit and converted the space into an extension of the traditional Apple Store. According to findings by MacRumors, this includes product walls along the walls used to display accessories, and redesigned display tables for showcasing Apple products.

The rest of the Apple Park Visitor Center, including the cafe, remains unchanged.

9to5Mac's Take

The AR experience at the Apple Park Visitor Center was certainly unique, but nine years later, it looks like the space has a better use.

I hope Apple isn't simply turning it into a generic retail store, but is thinking of other new ideas; at least the cafe is still around as a feature of the Apple Park Visitor Center.
